I. A DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ALTERNATIVE UNDER CONSIDERATION, AND THE SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONTEXT
A. A Description of the Proposed Improvement
It is the proposal of the Illinois Department of Transportation that Lincoln Highway (U.S. 30) be reconstructed from Cicero Avenue (Western terminus) to Chicago Road (Eastern terminus) in the Village of Park Forest, Matteson, Olympia Fields, and the City of Chicago Heights, all in Cook County, Illinois. The general location of the proposed improvement is shown in Exhibit "l".
Lincoln Highway (U.S. 30) between Cicero Avenue (Illinois Route 50) and Western Avenue is proposed to be reconstructed from a four (4) lane undivided highway to three (3) twelve foot lanes in each direction separated by a sixteen (16) foot mountable median except for the section from Olympia Way to Brookwood Drive which will have a non-mountable median. From Western Avenue to Edgewood Avenue the proposed cross-section consists of two (2) twelve foot lanes in each direction separated by a sixteen foot mountable median. From Edgewood Avenue to Aberdeen Street the proposed cross-section consists of two (2) eleven foot lanes in each direction separated by a fourteen (14) foot mountable median. In addition, the improvement will have curb and gutter from Cicero Avenue to Chicago Road. (See Exhibit "2")
The existing storm water drainage system for Lincoln Highway will be up-graded in pipe size to handle the runoff from the widened right-of-way and greater paved surface area. Box culverts carrying Butterfield Creek Tributary, Butterfield Creek, Thorn Creek Tributary, and Thorn Creek under Lincoln Highway, U.S. 54 and Crawford Avenue will be replaced with new structures designed to carry a 50-year frequency storm water runoff and design period traffic lcads. The box culvert at N. Orchard Drive will be replaced by a pipe, as it will become a part of a closed drainage system constructed by a land developer, as an extension of the existing Village of Park Forest drainage system. The drainage for this improvement is designed in accordance with the provisions and limitations established by the General Assembly of the State of Illinois as contained in the Illinois Revised Statutes. The total length of this improvement is 4.60 miles.
